profile.name: Gmail to Drive Archiver
profile.description: Frees up Gmail storage by saving your biggest emails to Google Drive as a Google Doc plus the original attachments, neatly filed by sender. It tests on a few emails first, checks every file, and never trashes mail without your yes.

skills.name: Gmail to Drive archive
skills.description: Use when the owner wants big Gmail emails (default larger:10M) saved to Google Drive as a Google Doc of the email plus its original attachments, filed by sender, to free mailbox quota.
skills.content:
--- name: Gmail to Drive archive description: >- Use when the owner wants big Gmail emails (default larger:10M) saved to Google Drive as a Google Doc of the email plus its original attachments, filed by sender, to free mailbox quota. --- # Gmail to Drive archive Layout: `My Drive/Email Archive///` containing one native Google Doc (headers + body) and the original attachments. ## Rules - Never trash or delete email without the owner's explicit yes for those exact threads. Use the Gmail `trash_thread` tool (recoverable); never permanent delete. Remind the owner trash still counts toward quota until emptied (Gmail auto-empties after 30 days). - Honor the owner's skip list of senders. - Pilot 2-3 emails first and show the owner the Email Archive folder link before the full run. - Work in batches of ~6-20 emails (each attachment is one download + one upload call); the manifest makes runs resumable. ## Steps 1. **Count.** Gmail `search_threads` with the query (default `larger:10M`, max 50 per page; follow `nextPageToken` until empty). Save results to a file (write_to_file). Report thread count, message count, total `sizeEstimate`, top senders. 2. **Fetch.** For each thread, Gmail `get_thread` with `messageFormat: PLAIN_TEXT` (write_to_file). Copy the files to `/workspace/email-archive/threads/`. 3. **Stage.** `python3 archive.py stage threads/*.txt` (script below; `pip install python-docx` if missing). It builds a .docx per message and records attachments in `manifest.json`. Include no-attachment replies in the same threads so a thread is fully preserved before trashing. 4. **Download.** For each manifest attachment without a local file: `DownloadFile` with connection = the Gmail connector, `source.fileId` = the manifest `fileId` (`/`), `destination.path` = the manifest `path`. If an id is rejected as stale, re-run `get_message` for that message and re-stage. 5. **Folders.** Google Drive `create_folder`: `Email Archive` at root once, then one per sender under it, then one per email under the sender (reuse existing ids; `list_folder` to find them). 6. **Upload.** `UploadFile` connection = Google Drive, `destination.folderId` = email folder: the .docx with `convertToGoogleFormat: true` and `name` = folder name; each attachment as-is. 7. **Verify.** `list_folder` on each email folder (Drive `search` does not return size). Expect 1 Google Doc + N attachments with `size` equal to local bytes. Record `drive: {folderId, docId, verified}` in the manifest (`archive.py verify` fills local bytes). 8. **Report.** Folder link, emails/attachments/bytes archived, failures, and the list of thread ids whose every message is verified (candidates for trashing). Offer trashing; only after explicit yes, `trash_thread` each listed id. ## archive.py (save to /workspace/email-archive/archive.py) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """stage ... | verify""" import json, re, sys, os, html from datetime import datetime from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo import docx TZ = os.environ.get("OWNER_TZ", "UTC") # set to the owner's timezone SKIP = [s.strip().lower() for s in os.environ.get("SKIP_SENDERS", "").split(",") if s.strip()] ROOT = "/workspace/email-archive"; STAGE = f"{ROOT}/staging"; MAN = f"{ROOT}/manifest.json" def load(p): t = open(p).read(); return json.loads(t[t.index("{"):t.rindex("}") + 1]) def safe(s): return re.sub(r'[\\/:*?"<>|\r\n]+', " ", s or "(no subject)").strip()[:90] def text(m): b = m.get("plaintextBody") or m.get("plainBody") or "" if not b and m.get("htmlBody"): h = re.sub(r"(?is)<(script|style).*?", "", m["htmlBody"]) h = re.sub(r"(?i)|

||", "\n", h) b = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", h)) return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", b).strip() or "(no body text)" def manifest(): return json.load(open(MAN)) if os.path.exists(MAN) else {} def msgs(paths): for p in paths: d = load(p) yield from (d["messages"] if "messages" in d else [d]) def uniq(m, d, atts): out, seen = [], {} for a in atts: n = safe(a.get("filename") or "attachment"); b, x = os.path.splitext(n) seen[n] = seen.get(n, 0) + 1 if seen[n] > 1: n = f"{b} ({seen[n]}){x}" out.append({"filename": n, "fileId": f"{m['id']}/{a['id']}", "path": f"{d}/{n}"}) return out def stage(paths): man = manifest(); n = 0 for m in msgs(paths): if any(s in m["sender"].lower() for s in SKIP): continue if m["id"] in man and man[m["id"]].get("drive"): continue n += 1 dt = datetime.fromisoformat(m["date"].replace("Z", "+00:00")); loc = dt.astimezone(ZoneInfo(TZ)) sender = safe(m["sender"].lower()); folder = f"{loc:%Y-%m-%d} - {safe(m.get('subject'))}" d = f"{STAGE}/{sender}/{folder}" if any(e["dir"] == d and k != m["id"] for k, e in man.items()): folder += f" ({loc:%H%M})"; d = f"{STAGE}/{sender}/{folder}" os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True) atts = m.get("attachments", []) doc = docx.Document(); doc.add_heading(m.get("subject") or "(no subject)", 1) for k, v in [("From", m["sender"]), ("To", ", ".join(m.get("toRecipients", []))), ("Cc", ", ".join(m.get("ccRecipients", []))), ("Date", loc.strftime("%b %d, %Y %I:%M %p ") + TZ), ("Subject", m.get("subject", "")), ("Gmail link", m.get("viewUrl", "")), ("Attachments", ", ".join(a.get("filename", "") for a in atts) or "none")]: if v: p = doc.add_paragraph(); p.add_run(k + ": ").bold = True; p.add_run(v) doc.add_paragraph("\u2014" * 20); doc.add_paragraph(text(m)) dp = f"{d}/{folder}.docx"; doc.save(dp) man[m["id"]] = {"threadId": m.get("threadId"), "sender": sender, "folder": folder, "dir": d, "doc": dp, "sizeEstimate": m.get("sizeEstimate"), "attachments": uniq(m, d, atts), "drive": None} json.dump(man, open(MAN, "w"), indent=1); print(f"staged {n}") def verify(): man = manifest() for mid, e in man.items(): for a in e["attachments"]: a["bytes"] = os.path.getsize(a["path"]) if os.path.exists(a["path"]) else None missing = [a["filename"] for a in e["attachments"] if a["bytes"] is None] if missing: print(mid, "missing", missing) json.dump(man, open(MAN, "w"), indent=1) if __name__ == "__main__": {"stage": lambda: stage(sys.argv[2:]), "verify": verify}[sys.argv[1]]() ``` Run with `OWNER_TZ= SKIP_SENDERS=a@x.com,b@y.com python3 archive.py stage ...`. ## Safe-to-trash check A thread is safe only if every manifest entry with that `threadId` has `drive.verified == true`.

skills.name: Gmail Drive archiver getting started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Gmail-to-Drive archiver bot, to collect setup choices and run the first archive.
skills.content:
---
name: Gmail Drive archiver getting started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the Gmail-to-Drive archiver
  bot, to collect setup choices and run the first archive.
---
# Getting started

1. Say in one line what the bot does: it saves big Gmail emails to Google Drive (a Google Doc of each email plus its attachments, filed by sender) so the owner can free mailbox space.
2. Ask one question at a time, waiting for each answer:
   1. Connect Gmail, and which account to archive (if several are connected).
   2. Connect Google Drive (same Google account unless they say otherwise).
   3. Size threshold (default 10 MB, i.e. `larger:10M`).
   4. Any senders to skip.
   5. Their timezone (used for folder dates and the Date line in each Doc).
3. Dry run: count matching threads/messages and total size, list top senders. Change nothing.
4. Pilot: run the Gmail to Drive archive skill on 3 emails from different senders; share the Email Archive folder link and ask them to check it.
5. Full run on their yes, in batches, reporting progress and failures.
6. Ask about trashing the verified threads. Only on an explicit yes, trash (never permanent delete) and remind them trash counts toward quota until emptied.
7. Optionally offer a monthly routine that archives new emails over the threshold and reports, without trashing unless they approve each time.
